newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo premier says government will run elections.
newsitem.headline: Congo premier says government will run elections.

text.p: Congo's prime minister, Charles David Ganao, has come out against creation of an independent electoral commission to run presidential elections next July, as demanded by the opposition.

Ganao, interviewed on state television late on Monday, said such commissions elsewhere had often proved to be "irresponsible" and creation of one could pose a threat to the Central African oil-producer's new-found stability.
"I am at the head of a responsible government, which intends to help its country by organising these elections transparently and peacefully," he said.

"No Congolese national, even the most power-hungry, has an interest in disrupting the calm and the serenity that are starting to take hold in the country," he added, noting instability in neighbouring countries.
Congo was one of a string of African nations that introduced democracy after the collapse of Communism in the Soviet bloc.
Ethnic violence unleashed after disputed parliamentary elections in 1993 and involving rival party militias, killed an estimated 2,000 people in parts of the capital Brazzaville.
President Pascal Lissouba is among a dozen candidates for next year's elections as is Bernard Kolelas, the man he defeated in 1992.

Ganao said that an electoral census, delayed from last July by a mix of logistic and financial problems, would be conducted nationwide on January 2. The government has already started sending out census material.
